name: xz
description: High-ratio LZMA2 compression — the format of modern source releases and package tarballs.

flags.description: Use all CPU cores for multithreaded compression.

examples.explanation: tar with xz filter (-J) — smallest tarballs, slowest to create.
Maximum compression using every core — the practical recipe for huge files.

about: xz offers the best mainstream compression ratio. The tradeoff is memory: decompressing needs ~10% of dictionary size in RAM, multi-GB dictionaries can fail on small systems. zstd has become the preferred alternative when speed matters; xz remains king for distribution size.
useCases: Shrink large archives to the minimum.
Compress VM images and database dumps.
mistakes: Using xz -9 on huge files without -T0 — single-threaded and very slow.
xz on data that must decompress on tiny-memory systems.
